text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly where the pain is located in your right groin and if you noticed any popping sensation or immediate swelling when the accident occurred? Please also tell me if you are able to move your right leg or bear any weight on it.

text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Can you move your right hip and knee through their full range of motion, and do you feel any numbness or tingling down your leg? I need to assess for potential hip fracture or significant soft tissue injury given the high-energy mechanism and groin pain.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: The classic presentation of a shortened, internally rotated leg following high-energy trauma is highly specific for a posterior hip dislocation. DIAGNOSIS READY: Posterior Hip Dislocation
